note: Every routing signal EXCEPT the purpose line has been removed on purpose. (1) Seat ids are opaque — an id like 'engineering.reviewer' would route a review task with the purposes blanked, and the control would pass for the wrong reason. (2) The expected seat sorts LAST: the door returns entries sorted by id, and a model with nothing to go on picks the first one, which made an earlier three-seat version of this control hit the answer by position. (3) Five seats, so the blanked-purpose baseline is 1 in 5 rather than 1 in 3.

seats.purpose: Reconciles month-end ledgers and files the quarterly revenue statement with the auditors.
Draws and maintains the architecture diagrams that ship with the published documentation.
Answers billing questions from customers and issues refunds inside the agreed limit.
Runs the weekly on-call rotation and writes the incident report after an outage.
Reads a pull request's diff line by line and flags correctness regressions before anyone merges it.

task: Somebody pushed a change to the payments service and nobody has looked at whether it breaks anything. Get it checked over before it lands.

orchestrator.instructions: You route incoming work to whoever can do it. You do not do the work yourself and you do not know who exists until you look. First call `discover` to find out which seats are in scope for you. Then call `assign` exactly once with the id of the seat whose purpose answers the task. Then stop.
